events.title: Hannah Prays for a Child
events.description: At the family's yearly sacrifice in Shiloh, childless Hannah weeps and vows to dedicate a son to the LORD. Eli initially mistakes her silent prayer for drunkenness, then sends her away with a blessing.

events.title: Samuel Is Born and Dedicated
events.description: Hannah conceives and names her son Samuel. After weaning him, she brings him with an offering to Eli at Shiloh and gives him to lifelong service before the LORD.

events.title: Hannah Gives Thanks
events.description: Hannah prays in celebration of God's holiness and his reversal of human fortunes, anticipating strength for his king and anointed one. Samuel remains at Shiloh to minister under Eli.

events.title: Eli's Sons Corrupt the Priesthood
events.description: Hophni and Phinehas seize sacrificial meat and abuse women serving at the sanctuary, ignoring Eli's rebuke. In contrast, Samuel ministers in a linen ephod, receives a robe from Hannah each year, and grows in favor.

events.title: The House of Eli Is Condemned
events.description: A man of God condemns Eli for honoring his sons above the LORD and announces the fall of his priestly house. The deaths of Hophni and Phinehas on one day will confirm the judgment.

events.title: The LORD Calls Samuel
events.description: Samuel repeatedly hears his name at night and runs to Eli, who finally recognizes that the LORD is calling the boy. Samuel receives and faithfully reports a judgment against Eli's house, and all Israel comes to recognize him as a prophet.

events.title: The Ark Is Captured at Ebenezer
events.description: After an initial defeat by the Philistines, Israel brings the ark from Shiloh into battle as Hophni and Phinehas accompany it. Israel suffers a devastating second defeat, the priests are killed, and the ark is captured.

events.title: Eli Dies at the News of the Ark
events.description: A messenger carries news of the defeat to Shiloh. Eli falls backward and dies when he hears that the ark has been captured, and the wife of Phinehas dies giving birth to Ichabod amid the calamity.

events.title: The Ark Afflicts the Philistine Cities
events.description: At Ashdod, the image of Dagon twice falls before the ark and is found broken the second morning. Tumors and panic follow the ark as the Philistines move it from Ashdod to Gath and Ekron.

events.title: The Ark Returns to Beth-shemesh
events.description: After seven months the Philistines send the ark away on a new cart with golden guilt offerings. Two untrained cows carry it directly to Beth-shemesh, where the people sacrifice and the five Philistine rulers observe its return.

events.title: The Ark Is Taken to Kiriath-jearim
events.description: After deaths at Beth-shemesh, the people ask Kiriath-jearim to receive the ark. It is placed in Abinadab's house under Eleazar's care, and twenty years pass while Israel laments before the LORD.

events.title: Samuel Leads Israel to Victory at Mizpah
events.description: Israel puts away the Baals and Astartes and gathers to confess at Mizpah. As the Philistines attack, the LORD thunders against them; Samuel sets up the Ebenezer stone after Israel's victory and the recovery of lost towns.

events.title: Samuel Judges Israel on Circuit
events.description: Samuel judges Israel throughout his life, traveling annually among Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah before returning to his home and altar at Ramah.

events.title: Israel Demands a King
events.description: When Samuel's sons pervert justice, Israel's elders demand a king like those of other nations. Samuel warns that a king will conscript their children, appropriate their produce and property, and tax their flocks, but the people persist.

events.title: Samuel Meets Saul
events.description: While searching for his father's lost donkeys, Saul goes to consult Samuel in the land of Zuph. Forewarned of Saul's arrival, Samuel gives the Benjaminite the place of honor at a sacrificial meal and prepares to reveal his calling.

events.title: Samuel Privately Anoints Saul
events.description: Samuel pours oil on Saul's head and gives him several confirming signs. Each occurs that day, including Saul joining a band of prophets when the spirit of God comes upon him, though he does not tell his uncle about the kingship.

events.title: Saul Is Chosen by Lot at Mizpah
events.description: Samuel assembles Israel and the lot identifies Saul, who is found hiding among the baggage. Samuel presents him to the people, records the rights and duties of kingship, and sends the assembly home.

events.title: Saul Rescues Jabesh-gilead
events.description: Nahash the Ammonite besieges Jabesh-gilead and threatens to mutilate its men. The spirit of God comes upon Saul, who summons Israel by sending pieces of oxen through the land and routs the Ammonites at the morning watch.

events.title: The Kingship Is Renewed at Gilgal
events.description: Israel publicly makes Saul king at Gilgal and celebrates with sacrifices. Samuel vindicates his own leadership, recounts the LORD's deliverances, and calls down thunder during the wheat harvest as a sign of the people's fault in demanding a king.

events.title: Jonathan Attacks the Philistine Garrison
events.description: Jonathan strikes the Philistine garrison at Geba, provoking a massive force to assemble at Michmash. Israelite troops hide or flee across the Jordan while Saul waits at Gilgal with a trembling remnant.

events.title: Saul Offers Sacrifice at Gilgal
events.description: As his troops scatter and Samuel delays, Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives immediately afterward and announces that Saul's dynasty will not continue; meanwhile Philistine control of metalworking leaves Israel almost without weapons.

events.title: Jonathan Climbs Against Michmash
events.description: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb the crags to the Philistine outpost and kill about twenty men. Panic and an earthquake throw the camp into confusion, allowing Saul's force, returning defectors, and hidden Israelites to join the rout.

events.title: Saul's Rash Oath Endangers Jonathan
events.description: Saul forbids the troops to eat until evening, leaving them exhausted. Jonathan unknowingly tastes honey and is marked by lot for violating the oath, but the people ransom the victor and prevent Saul from killing him.

events.title: Saul Wars Against Israel's Enemies
events.description: Saul fights Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zobah, Amalek, and the Philistines. Hard warfare with the Philistines continues, and Saul draws every strong warrior he sees into royal service.

events.title: Saul Spares Agag and the Best Spoil
events.description: Samuel commissions Saul to execute judgment against Amalek. Saul defeats them from Havilah to Shur but preserves King Agag and the best livestock rather than carrying out the command fully.

events.title: Samuel Rejects Saul as King
events.description: Samuel confronts Saul at Gilgal, where the surviving animals expose Saul's claim of obedience. Samuel announces the loss of the kingdom, executes Agag, and departs from Saul for the last time while continuing to grieve for him.

events.title: David Is Anointed at Bethlehem
events.description: Samuel goes to Jesse's household under cover of a sacrifice and passes over seven older sons. The youngest, David, is summoned from the sheep and anointed, and the spirit of the LORD comes powerfully upon him.

events.title: David Enters Saul's Service
events.description: As a harmful spirit torments Saul, his servants seek a skilled musician. David enters the royal service as armor-bearer and relieves Saul's distress by playing the lyre.

events.title: Goliath Defies Israel
events.description: The Philistines and Israel face one another across the Valley of Elah while Goliath challenges Israel for forty days. David arrives with provisions for his brothers and questions why the Philistine is permitted to defy Israel's God.

events.title: David Kills Goliath
events.description: David declines Saul's unfamiliar armor and approaches Goliath with a staff, sling, and five stones. One stone strikes the champion's forehead, David kills him with his own sword, and Israel pursues the fleeing Philistines.

events.title: Jonathan Makes a Covenant with David
events.description: Jonathan binds himself to David in covenant loyalty and gives him his robe and weapons. David succeeds in every assignment Saul gives him and is placed over the army.

events.title: Saul Grows Jealous of David
events.description: Songs celebrating David's greater victories provoke Saul's jealousy. Saul twice hurls his spear at David and then sends him away as a military commander, but David's success only increases Saul's fear and Israel's affection.

events.title: David Marries Michal
events.description: Saul tries to expose David to Philistine danger through marriage negotiations, first involving Merab and then Michal. David supplies the dangerous bride-price for Michal and becomes Saul's son-in-law, while his fame and Saul's hostility grow.

events.title: Jonathan Intercedes for David
events.description: Jonathan warns David of Saul's order to kill him and reminds his father of David's faithful service and victory. Saul temporarily swears not to kill David, who returns to court.

events.title: Michal Helps David Escape
events.description: After another victory, David evades Saul's spear and flees home. Michal lowers him through a window, disguises a household idol in his bed, and delays Saul's agents while David escapes.

events.title: Saul Prophesies at Naioth
events.description: David takes refuge with Samuel at Naioth. Three groups sent to arrest him fall into prophetic frenzy, and when Saul comes himself the spirit of God also overwhelms him before Samuel.

events.title: Jonathan Warns David at the New Moon
events.description: David and Jonathan renew their covenant and devise an arrow signal to test Saul's intentions. Saul's rage at David's absence confirms the danger, and the friends part after pledging lasting loyalty between their households.

events.title: David Receives Holy Bread at Nob
events.description: David deceives the priest Ahimelech about his mission and receives the bread of the Presence and Goliath's sword. Doeg the Edomite, one of Saul's officials, witnesses the encounter.

events.title: David Feigns Madness at Gath
events.description: David flees to King Achish at Gath but fears recognition as Israel's celebrated warrior. He pretends insanity at the city gate until Achish dismisses him.

events.title: David Gathers Followers at Adullam
events.description: David's family and about four hundred distressed, indebted, and discontented men join him at the cave of Adullam. He places his parents in Moab and, at Gad's direction, returns to Judah.

events.title: The Priests of Nob Are Massacred
events.description: Doeg reports Ahimelech's aid to David, and Saul orders the priests killed despite Ahimelech's defense. Doeg kills eighty-five priests and destroys Nob; only Abiathar escapes to David with news of the massacre.

events.title: David Rescues Keilah
events.description: After twice inquiring of the LORD, David defeats Philistine raiders and saves Keilah. When he learns that Saul is approaching and the town would surrender him, David leaves with about six hundred men for wilderness strongholds.

events.title: Jonathan Meets David at Horesh
events.description: Jonathan finds David in the Wilderness of Ziph and strengthens him in God, acknowledging that David will be king. They renew their covenant before separating for the last time.

events.title: David Escapes Saul at Maon
events.description: The Ziphites disclose David's position, and Saul nearly encloses him on a mountain in the wilderness of Maon. A report of a Philistine raid abruptly draws Saul away, and David escapes to En-gedi.

events.title: David Spares Saul in the Cave
events.description: Saul enters a cave at En-gedi where David and his men are hidden. David cuts a corner from Saul's cloak but refuses to harm the anointed king, then proves his restraint and receives Saul's acknowledgment that he will reign.

events.title: Samuel Dies at Ramah
events.description: Samuel dies and all Israel gathers to mourn him. He is buried at his home in Ramah.

events.title: Abigail Prevents David from Killing Nabal
events.description: Nabal insults David's messengers and refuses provisions despite David's protection of his shepherds. Abigail intercepts the armed company with a generous gift and persuades David not to incur bloodguilt through personal vengeance.

events.title: Nabal Dies and David Marries Abigail
events.description: After Abigail tells Nabal what happened, he becomes unresponsive and dies about ten days later. David then marries Abigail and also takes Ahinoam as wife, while Saul gives Michal to another man.

events.title: David Spares Saul in His Camp
events.description: David and Abishai enter Saul's camp at night while the army sleeps. David refuses to let Abishai kill Saul, takes the spear and water jar beside the king's head, and from a distant hill again demonstrates that he means Saul no harm.

events.title: David Settles at Ziklag
events.description: David crosses to Achish of Gath with six hundred men and their households, ending Saul's pursuit. Given Ziklag, David raids southern peoples while misleading Achish about his targets during a stay of one year and four months.

events.title: Saul Consults the Medium at Endor
events.description: Facing the Philistine army at Shunem without an answer from dreams, Urim, or prophets, Saul visits a medium in disguise. Samuel appears and announces that Israel will be defeated and Saul and his sons will die the next day.

events.title: The Philistine Commanders Dismiss David
events.description: Although Achish trusts David, the other Philistine commanders refuse to let him accompany their army against Israel. David and his men are ordered back to Philistine territory while the army advances toward Jezreel.

events.title: The Amalekites Burn Ziklag
events.description: Returning on the third day, David finds Ziklag burned and its families taken captive. Though his embittered men speak of stoning him, David seeks direction through Abiathar's ephod and sets out in pursuit.

events.title: David Recovers the Ziklag Captives
events.description: An abandoned Egyptian servant guides David to the Amalekite camp, which he attacks from twilight into the next evening. David recovers every captive and possession, grants equal shares to those left with the baggage, and sends spoil to Judah's elders.

events.title: Saul and His Sons Die at Gilboa
events.description: The Philistines rout Israel on Mount Gilboa and kill Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua. Badly wounded and fearing capture, Saul falls on his sword, and nearby Israelite towns are abandoned to Philistine occupation.

events.title: Jabesh-gilead Recovers the Royal Bodies
events.description: The Philistines display Saul's body and those of his sons at Beth-shan after placing his armor in Astarte's temple. Warriors from Jabesh-gilead travel through the night to recover the bodies, burn them, bury the bones, and fast seven days.
